evidence: No git tag exists in Argine2 marking a frozen/release commit (`git tag -l` is empty).

Argine2's HEAD (406763361a49a2c7ab6cbb811655dbdc51e77f9b, commit message 'Document public snapshot provenance') is a clean working tree at the tip of the only branch (master); there is no later commit.

Argine2's CITATION.cff records version '0.2.0' with date-released '2026-10-17', matching the date of HEAD and of the immediately preceding commit 707c088 ('Bind release metadata to public repository'), which added that version/date-released metadata.

Argine2's README.md Roadmap section states the publication experiment campaign is complete and the experiment registry contains no RUNNING or PLANNED experiments, consistent with treating this commit as the frozen Research Part 1 baseline.

No second, equally plausible candidate commit exists: Argine2 has a single branch and no tags, so HEAD is the only candidate, and the above evidence (tier 2 in the required priority order: an explicit commit documented as the frozen baseline) resolves it without ambiguity.

argine2_working_tree_at_inspection_time.note: A later git status (before Argine3 was created) found Argine2's HEAD unchanged (still 406763361a49a2c7ab6cbb811655dbdc51e77f9b) but ~1112 tracked files showing as modified in the working tree, due to a CRLF/LF line-ending mismatch between the committed blobs and the on-disk files. File mtimes on every affected file examined predate this task (most around 2026-10-03..2026-10-11, all well before 2026-11-07), confirming this is pre-existing drift, not a change made by this task. Argine3 was created by `git clone` of Argine2's .git object database only, which is unaffected by working-tree content; Argine2 itself was not written to at any point.
